title: Faneuil Hall managers sue tenants over more than $2 million in alleged unpaid rent
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: J. Safra Real Estate has sued seven tenants for over $2 million in alleged unpaid rent at Faneuil Hall.
The lawsuits were filed between July 2024 and July 2026 in Suffolk Superior Court, affecting mostly vacated businesses.
Faneuil Hall faces challenges with vacancies as management pursues renovations and new tenants like Tree House Brewing.

title: Do you really need a 4-year degree to build a career in Mass.?
author: Pattie Hunt Sinacole
bullets: Massachusetts' job market is shifting towards valuing skills and experience over a four-year degree due to rising college costs.
Healthcare and skilled trades are growth sectors with high demand for roles not requiring a bachelor's degree.
AI and technology advancements are changing job requirements, prompting employers to reconsider degree prerequisites.

title: Mike Vrabel: Drake Maye is not expected to play in preseason opener
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye is not expected to play in the preseason opener against the Colts.
Head coach Mike Vrabel said joint practices allow starters like Maye to get reps without preseason game contact.
Backup quarterbacks Tommy DeVito and rookie Behren Morton may see extended playtime in Maye's absence.

title: Seth Meyers runs Martha’s Vineyard road race with his son
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Seth Meyers and his son Ashe ran the Chilmark Road Race 5K on Martha's Vineyard.
Meyers finished fifth in his division, averaging 7:30 per mile during the race.
Meyers frequently visits Martha's Vineyard, where he owns a home in Chilmark.

title: Explaining the controversy that caused a lengthy delay in the Red Sox-Blue Jays game
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: The Red Sox-Blue Jays game featured a rare 'fourth out' scenario prompting a lengthy rules review.
A scoreboard error misled players into believing there were two outs, affecting Boston's baserunning decisions.
Umpires ruled a Red Sox run valid as Toronto failed to make an appeal play before leaving the field.

title: Bicyclist taken to hospital by helicopter after crash with vehicle in North Andover
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Bicyclist seriously injured in crash with vehicle at 100 Turnpike St., North Andover.
Injured bicyclist, an adult male, airlifted to a regional trauma center.
Driver of the vehicle involved in the crash was unharmed.

title: This new board game turns the MBTA experience into a game
author: Gwen Egan
bullets: Michelle Dundek from Malden created 'Mass Transit,' a board game inspired by her experiences on Boston's subway system.
The objective is to collect cards representing stations, simulating the unpredictable nature of the MBTA.
Dundek's game gained popularity after a viral video, selling out of her handmade copies quickly.

title: Suspicious death investigation underway at N.H. mobile home park
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: A suspicious death is being investigated at Hilltop Manor mobile home park in Whitefield, New Hampshire.
Three family members were injured and treated at local hospitals following the incident.
The investigation is led by the New Hampshire State Police’s major crime unit and Attorney General John Formella’s office.

title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial continues with more testimony from psychiatric NP
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Lindsay Clancy's trial features testimony from psychiatric nurse practitioners Julie Paul and Rebecca Jollotta about her mental health treatment.
Judge William Sullivan considers allowing testimony from a former McLean Hospital social worker on holiday staffing and conditions.
Clancy, charged with murdering her three children, pleads not guilty by reason of insanity, citing postpartum mental illness.

title: Local obituary: Max Rothschild, Williamstown 7-year-old
author: Boston.com Staff
bullets: Max Rothschild, a 7-year-old from Williamstown, died on August 7 after being hit by a car while riding his bike.
Rothschild was known for his love of math, chess, soccer, swimming, skiing, and adventures like ziplines and ropes courses.
Funeral services will be held at Congregation Beth Israel in North Adams, with burial at Beth Israel Cemetery in Clarksburg.
